items.stem: Why does modeling metrics in LookML help an organization?

options.text: It defines metrics once so every report uses a consistent definition
options.rationale: Correct: the modeling layer centralizes metric definitions for consistency.

options.text: It copies the warehouse data into Looker for speed
options.rationale: Looker queries the warehouse; it does not store its own copy.

options.text: It removes the need for a data warehouse
options.rationale: Looker sits on top of a warehouse; it does not replace it.

options.text: It makes all dashboards load instantly without tuning
options.rationale: Performance still requires caching and modeling choices.

items.explanation: Correct: the LookML modeling layer gives consistent, reusable metric definitions.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO help a slow Looker dashboard perform better? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: datagroups cache results and reduce repeated warehouse queries.

options.text: Use aggregate awareness to query smaller rollup tables
options.rationale: Correct: aggregate awareness routes queries to pre-aggregated tables.

options.text: Remove all joins so nothing can be analyzed
options.rationale: Removing needed joins breaks the analysis, not a valid fix.

options.text: Disable caching so data is always refetched
options.rationale: Disabling caching increases load, worsening performance.

items.explanation: Correct: datagroup caching and aggregate awareness both improve dashboard performance.

items.stem: A view is joined to another on a many-to-one relationship but declared as one-to-one. What is the likely result?

options.rationale: Correct: a wrong join relationship can fan out rows and inflate aggregates.

options.text: Faster query performance with no downside
options.rationale: An incorrect relationship causes wrong numbers, not a safe speedup.

options.text: Looker refuses to run any query
options.rationale: Looker will run it but return incorrect aggregates.
Looker does not silently fix a misdeclared relationship.

items.explanation: Correct: a misdeclared join relationship can inflate measures through row fan-out.
